chunks: Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd narrated from Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Askari (peace be upon him)
about a man who made a bequest of wealth in the way of Allah, so he said: 'The way of Allah is our Shia.'
ai.seo_question: What does 'in the way of Allah' mean for bequests according to Imam Al-Askari?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*, Imam Ali ibn Muhammad (Al-Askari) redefines 'fi sabeelillah' not merely as general charity but specifically as the Shia (followers) of the Ahl al-Bayt, establishing a theological link between material support and religious identity. This interpretation underscores the Shia view that sustaining the community of the Imams is the highest form of spending in the way of Allah, distinct from broader Islamic charitable categories.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5478 - Muhammad bin Isa bin Ubaid narrated from Al-Hasan bin Rashid, who said:
I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Askari, (Imam Ali ibn Muhammad Al-Hadi (as))

about a man who made a will to dedicate wealth "in the way of Allah (swt)" (fi sabeelillah).
Imam (as) replied: "The way of Allah (swt) is our Shia (followers)."
